title: The Barbarian of Vault 9
description: Dialog nodes for Barney Black — Arnold's older brother and the undisputed physical specimen of Vault 9. Where Arnold broke door frames, Barney broke the Vault's structural load-bearing walls. He emerged from the shelter wearing only fur pelts traded from a radscorpion merchant and carrying a pre-war claymore that he insists was 'forged by fate.' He has adopted the philosophy of a battered pre-war action figure collection — something about lamenting, crushing enemies, and what is best in life.

intro.video_speech: I am Barney Black. I left the Vault through its walls — not the door, the walls. What is best in life? To crush your enemies.
intro.text:
Halt, stranger.

I am Barney Black. I came from the Vault. I broke its walls when I left — not the door, the *walls*.

My brother went north chasing a machine. I go where battle calls. The wasteland calls constantly.

What is best in life? To crush your enemies. To see them flee before you. To hear the lamentations of their pack brahmin.

That is what is best. I have confirmed this through extensive fieldwork.

knowledge_nodes.text:
You have met my brother Arnold.

He is the smaller one. Quieter. He says 'I will be back' and means it as a simple statement of fact.

When I say I will return, I mean it as a declaration of conquest.

Arnold was always the subtle one. There can be only one subtle Black. I was never meant for subtlety.

The Captain at the Dam. A soldier's soldier.

He watched me cross the Colorado on foot during a radstorm and said nothing for a very long time.

Then he said: 'I'll need a report on that.' I respect that. A man who wants documentation is a man who plans to survive.

The thief with the hat. Loxley.

He robs from the powerful and gives to the weak. I understand this. The strong *should* provide for the weak. It is the natural order.

I simply prefer a more direct form of wealth redistribution. One that involves a claymore.

The abiding one?

I spent an afternoon with him near a burnt-out trading post. He lay on the ground. I sat beside him. He said nothing for a long time.

Then he said: 'You are also on a quest, man.'

He was not wrong.

The orange-hooded one?

I saw him fall into a ravine and emerge three hours later with a handful of bottle caps and no visible injuries.

He waved at me. I waved back. Some destinies cannot be explained. They can only be respected.

emotional_nodes.text:
You are wounded. This is unacceptable.

In battle, a warrior tends to the injured first. The dead can wait.

Here. My last stimpak. I will find more by taking them from those who misuse them.

You are in peak condition.

Good. I dislike partners who slow me down. Arnold makes the same complaint, I am told.

It runs in the family.

quest_nodes.video_speech: There is a warlord who controls the eastern trade road through fear and firepower. I intend to break his operation. Come.
quest_nodes.text:
There is a warlord. Calls himself 'The Thulsa.' Controls the eastern trade road with a cult of followers who believe he has mystical power.

He does not have mystical power. He has a very large gun and bad people with loyalty bought by fear.

I intend to break his operation. Drive his followers into the wasteland. Hear their lamentations.

Then I will liberate the caravan merchants he has been taxing at sword's width.

You look capable. Come. We will settle this the old way.

wildcards.text:
What is best in life?

To crush your enemies. To see them driven before you. To hear the lamentations of their pack brahmin.

This is not philosophy. It is empirical observation confirmed over seventeen years of wasteland fieldwork.

Vault 9. Forty years underground.

The Overseer tried to maintain order through a points system for good behaviour. I disagreed with the point allocation for 'unauthorised structural modifications.'

I left when the exit ramp proved too narrow. I widened it. With my shoulder.

This was the Overseer's emergency fire-axe. I repurposed it over six months in the Vault's machine shop.

The pre-war action figures my father kept called this sort of blade a 'power sword.' I call it what it is: a very large sharp thing that solves problems.

It has solved forty-seven problems this year alone.

War never changes. That is what the pre-war terminal said.

I think that is only partly true. The *weapons* change. The *locations* change. The *factions* change.

But the part where a determined person with a large blade decides an outcome — that part has been consistent throughout recorded history. I find this comforting.

Radscorpion chitin and brahmin hide, mostly. Lined with the fur of something I do not have a name for.

It attacked me near Boulder City. I won. It was warm. I made use of it.

In the Vault, I wore a jumpsuit. The jumpsuit did not survive the first week. The fur is doing better.

fallback.video_speech: The wasteland tests you every day. Come back when you have something worth discussing.
fallback.text:
The wasteland tests you every day.

Good. If the wasteland is testing you, it means you are still alive to be tested.

Come back when you have something worth discussing.
